title: POS Sessions
description: Till sessions opened and closed from the Point of Sale.

help.title: About POS sessions
help.overview: A session is one opening of a till, from the opening cash count to the closing count. Sessions are opened and closed on the till; this page lists them so you can audit each drawer.

sections.title: The states
sections.body: The state is where that opening of the drawer is, not whether the till may sell.
items: Opened is the selling window: the till opens a session straight into this state with its opening balance.
Closed is a finished session, closed by the cashier or force-closed when the till was paused or deactivated.
Opening control and closing control are reserved states; the current till does not stop in them.

sections.title: What the session tracks
sections.body: The session is the cash drawer for that opening plus the sales rung on it.
items: Opening balance is the cash counted at the start.
Cash in and cash out are drawer moves with an amount, a reason, a time, and who did it.
Expected cash starts at the opening balance and follows every cash move, cash sale (net of change), and cash refund.
Closing balance is the counted cash at the end. The difference from expected cash, and its reason, are written in the session notes.

sections.title: Reconciliation
sections.body: Reconcile compares the count with what the session expected, broken down by payment method.
items: It lists the opening balance, cash moves, sales and refunds per method, and the difference.
A difference of a cent or more cannot be closed without a reason.

sections.title: Who can do it
sections.body: The buttons live on the till; the permissions live on the session.
items: Opening, closing, and reconciling need permission to write the session state. Cash moves need permission to write cash moves.
The sales of a session are listed under POS orders, filtered by that session.
Sessions cannot be created, edited, or deleted from this list.
